//WHAT THIS IS: Configuration for pointing the .NET backend at the HOSTED PRODUCTION
database, read-only, to verify that the ported queries and column mappings
match the real schema and real data.
It carries NO credentials. Supply them at run time, so nothing secret is
ever committed:
set ConnectionStrings__HrPortal=Server=...;Database=...;User Id=...;Password=...
set ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=LiveReadOnly
dotnet run
USE A MYSQL ACCOUNT GRANTED SELECT ONLY. Not the application account.
The application account can INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE, and this codebase
writes to users, attendance, refresh_tokens and login_history in the normal
course of a login or a punch. A read-only grant means the SERVER refuses a
write, rather than the refusal depending on nobody calling the wrong
endpoint.
Create one on the host (run as an admin account, once):
CREATE USER 'hr_readonly'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY '<a long random password>';
GRANT SELECT ON db_ab2fe4_ems.* TO 'hr_readonly'@'%';
FLUSH PRIVILEGES;
Some shared hosting panels will not create a second MySQL user. If yours
will not, do NOT fall back to the application account: take a dump instead
(that is a read) and restore it locally.
Startup will refuse to continue unless the server confirms this connection
has no write privileges -- see SchemaSafetyGuard.
